message.text: The ownership guard in `TelemetryReader.round` has no test that reaches its rejecting branch. The guard returns nothing when the round has no verdict or when a later review has replaced the review index's adjudication task. The only test that reads real telemetry, in cli/test/compare.test.ts, has one review, and there the guard passes. The pipeline `no record` tests do not separate this guard from the missing round or the failed Changeset.resolve.

explanation.what: The ownership guard in `TelemetryReader.round` has no test that reaches its rejecting branch. The guard returns nothing when the round has no verdict or when a later review has replaced the review index's adjudication task. The only test that reads real telemetry, in cli/test/compare.test.ts, has one review, and there the guard passes. The pipeline `no record` tests do not separate this guard from the missing round or the failed Changeset.resolve.
explanation.whatToDo: Add a ComparisonCauses test that reviews a revision, adjudicates a valid miss, then runs a second review of the same revision so it replaces the index entry. Assert that the first round reads `no record`. Add a second case for a round with no verdict.
explanation.whyHere: This change adds the guard so that a round's first read never comes from a later review's telemetry. If the guard is wrong, the export prints a wrong cause that looks authoritative.

properties.failureScenario: Delete `|| !round.stored.tasks.some((task) => task === owner)`. Then a round whose revision a later review re-ran reads the later run's stages, and the export reports e.g. `seen, not reported` from the other run's prompt. Every test I read would still pass: no test in packages/pipeline/test calls `.round(` on TelemetryReader, and the cli test's one-review setup gives owner ∈ tasks either way.
